content: The World Health Organization (WHO) has published guidelines for the treatment of Neisseria gonorrhoeae, focusing on drug therapy and addressing issues related to antimicrobial resistance. The publication includes a summary of conflicts of interest and emphasizes that the designations and presentation of material do not imply any opinion on the legal status of countries, territories, cities, or their authorities, nor on the delimitation of their boundaries. Any dotted or dashed lines on maps represent approximate borders, which may not yet have full agreement. The mention of specific companies or manufacturers' products does not constitute endorsement or recommendation by WHO over others of a similar nature. Proprietary product names are distinguished by initial capital letters. WHO has taken all reasonable precautions to verify the information contained in the publication, but the material is distributed without warranty of any kind, either expressed or implied. The responsibility for the interpretation and use of the material lies with the reader, and WHO shall not be held liable for damages arising from its use. The document also includes a detailed summary of conflicts of interest for individuals involved in the development of the guidelines. This includes declarations of any related academic work, commercial financial interests, indirectly related commercial financial interests, and non-commercial interests or grants. For example: 1. No other conflicts of interest declared. 15. Amina El Kettani (Morocco): No conflicts of interest declared in any category. 16. The guidelines also provide a regional breakdown of contributors and their affiliations, ensuring transparency in the development process. WHO regions include the African Region (AFR), Region of the Americas (AMR), Eastern Mediterranean Region (EMR), European Region (EUR), South-East Asian Region (SEAR), and Western Pacific Region (WPR).
